title: Integration of Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy into Systemic Cancer Treatments for Metastatic Disease – Registry
summary:
Stereotactic radiotherapy (SBRT) complements systemic therapies for metastatic cancers and is generally safe and highly effective. SBRT has become a standard part of treatment.  However, questions remain: 1. Which patients benefit most from SBRT? 2. At what time point does SBRT achieve the best results? 3. Which metastases should best be targeted for radiation therapy?

The INTERACT Registry monitors patients scheduled for SBRT of extracranial tumor lesions. The registry will investigate the oncological course and treatment-related side effects of SBRT. In addition, advanced analyses of imaging data and blood tests will be conducted. In this way, we hope to gain a deeper understanding of the progression of different tumor types and treatments and thus improve treatment outcomes for patients with metastatic disease.
conditions: histologically confirmed solid malignancy with metastatic disease detected on imaging.

interventions.name: SBRT and systemic therapy will be applied as clinically indicated . Patients’ imaging data (clinical routine) and blood samples (study-specific) will be prospectively collected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	histologically confirmed solid malignancy with metastatic disease detected on imaging. Biopsy confirmation of metastatic disease is preferred but not required
•	one to ten extracranial active tumor lesions on recent imaging
•	local radiotherapy is clinically indicated and scheduled according to one of the INTERACT schemes 
•	ECOG 0/1
•	age ≥18 years
•	able and willing to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
•	serious medical comorbidities precluding ablative radiotherapy
•	substantial overlap of disease sites with a previously treated radiation volume that precludes meeting dose constraints in a composite plan
•	malignant meningitis
•	pregnant or lactating individuals 
•	patient’s refusal to participate
